name: Letter Comments
rows: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026 · Ledgerwyn, Vellumrow, Charterfold and Quillpost · IT general controls workpapers
DRAFT FOR THE CPA · audit procedures · not an audit report · no opinion on internal control
Administrator rights and manual entries · Material weakness, proposed, for the CPA to confirm

The Controller administers all four systems and posts entries; a shared Ledgerwyn administrator; a vendor administrator left enabled; 30 entries over $25,000, $8,045,083.44, posted with no second person; periods never locked.
The policy keeps administrator rights apart from transaction rights, allows no shared accounts and requires a second approval of entries over $25,000.
The Controller and Saltmarsh IT Services LLC, for upgrades and year-end work. We share the password; it was last changed in 2024.
Nothing in the systems prevents or records an override of the controls by the person who keeps the books.
Give user administration to someone who posts nothing, retire the shared account, disable the vendor account, turn on the approval step and lock each period at close.
To be written by management, with an owner and a date
Conflicting duties in payments and payroll · Significant deficiency, proposed, for the CPA to confirm

Mei Northcott sets up vendors and prepares and approves payments; she approved 4 of her own, $64,675.50. Renata Salazar edits the employee master and processes payroll and entered her own unsigned raise.
The policy: no one both sets up vendors and approves payments, creates and approves payments, or edits the payroll master and processes payroll.
When the bank portal was set up in 2023. We have not reviewed them since.
A fictitious vendor or an unapproved pay change could be paid without a second person.
Remove the AP Specialist’s approval right, have the Controller approve every vendor setup, run and sign the master file change report each payroll.
To be written by management, with an owner and a date
A change made without approval · Significant deficiency, proposed, with ITGC-02, for the CPA to confirm
VR-25-09 raised the AP Specialist’s approval limit to $25,000 with no ticket, test or CFO approval; $54,815.50 of self-approved payments were above the old limit.
The policy: every change to a financial system or its settings needs a ticket, a test and the CFO’s approval.
The Controller asked Vellumrow support by email so small payments would not wait for her. There was no ticket; the CFO was not asked.
A setting that controls who can release money changed with no one checking it.
Put every change, settings included, through the ticket, the test and the CFO.
To be written by management, with an owner and a date
Leavers still able to sign in · Deficiency, for the CPA to confirm
3 accounts of two leavers active on July 31, 2026; one mailbox used after the last day.
The policy: every account of a leaver disabled within 1 business day.
HR emails the Office Manager, who disables the Quillpost account. Ledgerwyn and Charterfold accounts are removed by their owners when they hear about it; there is no checklist.
A former employee could reach company email and job cost data.
Disable every account of a leaver on the last day from one checklist across all four systems.
To be written by management, with an owner and a date
Passwords and multi-factor sign-in · Deficiency, for the CPA to confirm
Ledgerwyn passwords of six characters with no lockout or multi-factor sign-in; 6 Quillpost accounts exempt from multi-factor sign-in.
The policy: 12 characters, a lockout after 5 failed sign-ins, multi-factor sign-in for every account.
The CEO and the AP Specialist found the codes slowed them down on their phones; the others were set up before we enforced it and were never added.
A guessed or stolen password opens the books, the payments or the email that approves them.
Enforce the password policy everywhere and multi-factor sign-in for every account, no exemptions.
